title: Safety floors
summary: Rules that stay on whatever else you choose: your identity in commits, safe deletes, secrets kept out of files.
why: Each floor exists because its absence once cost the author something that could not be recovered. They are shown and explained here, but they cannot be switched off.

items.title: Commits carry your identity only
items.does: Adds the rule that no commit or pull request carries an AI or bot co-author, sign-off or author.
items.why: Code hosts list a contributor for every identity in the default branch history, trailers included, and settings alone did not keep assistant identities out. The hooks that enforce this are in the attribution module.

items.title: Headless runs fail closed
items.does: Adds the rule that a background run with a missing or unreachable route is refused rather than rerouted.
items.why: A silent retry on the interactive login would bill the very account the separate headless route exists to protect, and nobody would notice until the quota ran out.
items.notes: Inert until the headless module is on; the spawn helper there enforces it.

items.title: Never stop running work to check on it
items.does: Adds the rule that status checks read progress files and never stop, restart or edit a running agent.
items.why: Looking at a running task by poking it has killed the task more than once; a progress file answers the same question without risk.

items.title: Irreplaceable deletes go to the Recycle Bin
items.does: Adds the rule that anything which cannot be regenerated is recycled or moved aside, never unlinked.
items.why: A direct delete of almost 10 GB once proved unrecoverable within the hour: no restore point, no shadow copy, no undelete. The Recycle Bin is the cheapest backup there is.

items.title: Reconfiguring scripts are never trial-run on this machine
items.does: Adds the rule that scripts which change system settings are reviewed and parse-checked here, and executed only on their target or in a sandbox.
items.why: A stubbed trial run once changed a real network and firewall setting because one command was not stubbed. Reading the script costs minutes; repairing the machine costs an evening.

items.title: Secrets are references, never values
items.does: Adds the rule that configuration points at where a secret lives, and that errors name the reference only.
items.why: A tracked document once held account emails and ids side by side. A file that never contains a secret cannot leak one, whatever happens to it later.

items.title: OS changes: backup, one change, read back
items.does: Adds the discipline for system and security settings: save the current state, change one thing, read it back, roll back on a regression.
items.why: When an agent touches the firewall, a network adapter or a service, the safety comes from being able to put it back exactly. Whether an agent may make such changes at all is a separate, opt-in item.
items.notes: Only the discipline ships here. Letting the agent apply OS changes itself is the item os-self-apply-grant, off by default.

items.title: Secret-reference helper
items.does: Copies kit_secrets.py, which resolves a secret from an environment variable, file or command and never prints the value, together with the kit's LICENSE and NOTICE.
items.why: Every tool that needs a token asks one helper, so no tool ever has a reason to read or log the raw value.

items.title: No telemetry
items.does: Adds the rule that nothing reports usage, prompts, files or errors anywhere, and that crash reports stay local until you send one.
items.why: The console and this profile run on your machine with your code and accounts. The only network calls are the update check and the ones you start yourself.
